title: improv·artist · obsessive (Yayoi Kusama)
mutation_directive: improv artist: obsessive via Yayoi Kusama

improv_extras.practice: infinite polka-dot repetition; pumpkins; mirror-room infinity; scale and pattern as obsession made visible

v1.feedback: The Kusama link lands — obsessive dot-tiling on a fleshy differential-growth tube is the right move, and the cadmium-red/cream palette is restrained and period-correct. Push further: the tube radius (0.38) is thin enough that the dot coverage reads more like beads-on-a-wire than Kusama's suffocating all-over pattern; fatten the tube or add secondary branching tendrils so dots dominate more surface area. The breathing pulse is too subtle at 0.08 amplitude — Kusama's repetition is anxious, not gentle, so consider staggering dot scale more aggressively or adding slight color drift (cream→yellow→cream) per ring to sell the compulsive quality. The piece entirely skips the pumpkin and infinity-mirror dimensions of the brief; even one gourd-like bulge in the growth curve or a reflective ground plane would strengthen the reference beyond generic dot-on-tube.

v2.feedback: The Kusama link lands well — differential-growth pumpkin form with obsessive cream-yellow polka dots on cadmium red is a legible homage, and the infinity-mirror ground plane is a smart nod to her mirror rooms. The gourd bulge logic and dot tiling give it real silhouette, not just noise. To refine: the dot density could increase as the form matures (obsession escalating over time), the palette drift between cream and yellow is subtle enough to read as monotone — push a few dots toward gold or even black for the iconic Kusama contrast, and the camera should auto-orbit slowly or frame tighter so the pumpkin dominates more of the canvas at rest. The ground mirror is a nice touch but currently competes for attention; dim it or tint it deeper red so the pumpkin stays the hero.
